text:
eva_ae: Heads-up - big bank wants EU primary + US hot-standby. Key asks: no non-cloud third-parties in standby path, SOC/ISO attestations for any infra partners, and a quick warm vs hot cost delta for proposal.

leo_se: Quick clarifying Qs - 1) If failover hits US, can we guarantee traffic stays inside AWS/Azure (no NetCrest)? 2) Would standby persist KV cache or be cold spin-up?

miriam_sre: TL;DR: If tenant peering enabled, traffic stays on peered path within their cloud account; otherwise public egress. For Dedicated with peering we avoid NetCrest. Standby modes: warm keeps KV/cache + minimal workers; hot mirrors full fleet.

tara_compliance: We'll export the sub-processor list and current cert status. AWS/Azure nodes covered; third-party partners have mixed attestations. Expect NetCrest ISO ETA ~5-7 weeks.

eva_ae: Sales needs a quick number - warm vs hot multiplier for committed capacity to include in SOW.

miriam_sre: Ballpark: warm ~1.12x, hot ~1.38x of baseline reserved. Bandwidth egress and peering charges extra. Provide model size and RPS for precision.

eva_ae: Can someone draft a simple routing policy to show deterministic failover only to us-west?

miriam_sre: Sample line: routing: primary=eu-central-1; standby=us-west-2; failover=manual; allow-fallback=false; peering-required=true

deploy-bot: Onboarding note: dedicated-peering pipeline ~3 business days after legal and CIDR.

leo_se: Action items: Tara - sub-processor CSV + cert ETAs to Eva by EOD. Miriam - refine warm/hot ranges (low/med/high) if Eva sends model RPS. Eva - confirm whether customer will accept Dedicated+peering or insists on Hosted-only.

eva_ae: I'll confirm with the customer and loop back. Thanks all :thumbsup:
